title: Versioned experiments
goals: Keep development checks separate from final evaluation

prerequisite.prompt: Why should expected test results be written before running the function?
prerequisite.answer: To avoid changing expectations simply to match a bug.

vocabulary: An identified state of code or rules
Cases used while choosing or improving a method
Cases reserved for an evaluation after choices are fixed

blocks.text: A fictional activity scoring experiment compares two weight settings on the same development records. Save code version, input version, weights, tie rule and outputs. A label such as v2 is useful only when it refers to an identifiable saved state.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
items = [{"name": "A", "fun": 4, "learning": 1},
         {"name": "B", "fun": 2, "learning": 4}]
for version, fun_weight, learning_weight in [("v1", 2, 1), ("v2", 1, 2)]:
    scores = []
    for item in items:
        scores.append(fun_weight * item["fun"]
                      + learning_weight * item["learning"])
    print(version, scores)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The ranking changes because the preference weights changed. That is a policy comparison, not proof that v2 is more accurate. Keep the same data and constraints when comparing weights, and record why a policy better fits the stated goal.

blocks.label: If the data also changes between v1 and v2, can the ranking change be attributed only to weights?

blocks.text: Overwriting a file called latest removes the ability to reproduce earlier results unless versions are retained elsewhere. Save identifiable versions and a run log. Avoid editing a reserved final test after seeing its output to make the chosen version look better.
Once holdout results guide another change, those cases have become development evidence. A later independent evaluation needs new reserved cases. Small holdouts still provide limited evidence.

blocks.label: You revise the policy after reading final-case failures. Are those cases still untouched holdout evidence?

workbook.title: Record a run
workbook.prompt: List five items needed to reproduce a scoring run.
workbook.answer: Code version, input version, configuration weights, tie/eligibility rules and outputs; also record date and method as useful context.

workbook.title: Compute a comparison
workbook.prompt: A has fun 3 and learning 2. Score it under weights (2,1) and (1,2).

workbook.title: Repair an experiment
workbook.prompt: A learner changes weights, input ratings and the time limit together. Why is attribution difficult?
workbook.answer: Multiple factors changed. Compare one deliberate change while holding the others fixed, or explicitly describe a multi-change experiment without attributing it to one cause.

workbook.title: Design independently
workbook.prompt: Plan two versions for C (fun 5, learning 1) and D (fun 2, learning 5), using weights (2,1) and (1,2). Record expected scores, ranks, fixed data and a separate final-case plan.
workbook.answer: v1 C 11, D 9 selects C; v2 C 7, D 12 selects D. Preserve the same records and other rules; reserve unseen cases until the policy is fixed.

workbook.title: Protect evaluation
workbook.prompt: You revise the policy after reading final-case failures. Are those cases still untouched holdout evidence?
workbook.answer: No. They now informed development. Report that use and seek fresh cases for a new independent check.

teacher.background: Teach Week 28 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional activity scoring experiment compares two weight settings on the same development records. Save code version, input version, weights, tie rule and outputs. A label such as v2 is useful only when it refers to an identifiable saved state. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.

teacher.assessment: Independent W4 evidence: v1 C 11, D 9 selects C; v2 C 7, D 12 selects D. Preserve the same records and other rules; reserve unseen cases until the policy is fixed. teacher.support: Provide a run-log table. Extension: rerun a saved version in a fresh folder and compare exact output values.
